items.item: Every status column heading shows the status name and its ticket count, and the count equals the cards shown or the column states how many are not shown (such as "Showing 20 of 134")
items.evidence:
header.innerHTML renders `

${status.label}

` next to `${colTickets.length}` (page.html:161-167); colTickets.length is the exact array that gets rendered as cards, so the count always equals the cards shown (e.g. 'New' shows 4 and exactly 4 cards render).

items.item: Each card shows the ticket number (such as #4821), subject, customer, priority as a word or code (such as "P1 · Urgent") and the assignee, or an explicit "Unassigned"
items.evidence: Card template (page.html:191-204) renders `${t.id}` (e.g. 'TCK-1042'), `${pr.label}` (e.g. 'Urgent'), `${escapeHtml(t.subject)}`, `${escapeHtml(t.customer)}`, and `${t.assignee}` which is literally the string 'Unassigned' for unassigned tickets (e.g. TCK-1044 in screenshot).

items.item: Open tickets show the time left to the next SLA target and which target it is (such as "Resolution due in 2h 15m"), and breached tickets show how long they are overdue (such as "Breached 40m ago") in text or with an icon, not by colour alone
items.evidence: slaInfo() (page.html:104-120) outputs only an absolute timestamp ('Due Nov 7, 2:00 PM' / 'Breached Nov 7, 11:00 AM') — never a countdown/elapsed duration like '2h 15m' or '40m ago', and never names which SLA target (first response vs. resolution) is being tracked; every status uses the same generic 'Due'/'Breached' wording.

items.item: Tickets in a waiting status (such as "Waiting on customer") show their SLA timer as paused instead of counting down
items.evidence: slaInfo(iso, status) only special-cases status 'resolved'/'closed' as done ('Met ...'); the 'pending' (Pending Customer) status falls through to the same due/breached branches as 'new'/'open' (page.html:108-119), so pending tickets like TCK-1020 still show a counting 'Due Nov 10, 5:00 PM' with no paused state.

items.item: Within each column the cards are ordered by SLA due time or by priority, and the board states which ordering is used
items.evidence: Cards render in raw array insertion order with no sort call anywhere in renderBoard(); e.g. the 'Pending Customer' column shows TCK-1020 (due Nov 10), TCK-1024 (due Nov 9), TCK-1027 (due Nov 7) — not ascending or descending by SLA, and not grouped by priority (Low, Medium, High). No text anywhere states an ordering rule.

items.item: Search finds tickets by number, subject or customer, and filters cover assignee (including "Me" and "Unassigned"), priority and SLA state (such as breached or due within 1 hour)
items.evidence: matchesFilter() (page.html:136-144) checks id/subject/customer for search — that part works — but the only other filter is #assignee-filter, populated from AGENTS (page.html:334-340) which includes 'Unassigned' but no 'Me' option tied to the current user (Jordan Mills); there is no priority filter and no SLA-state filter control anywhere in the markup.

items.item: Each card has keyboard-reachable actions to assign the ticket (including "Assign to me") and to change its status without dragging, with accessible names that include the ticket number
items.evidence: The card div has no tabindex/role/keydown handler, only `card.addEventListener('click', ...)` (page.html:207), so it cannot be reached or activated by keyboard. The modal's assignee/status controls are plain `<select>` elements with generic labels ('Assignee', 'Status', page.html:288-301) with no accessible name referencing the ticket number, and there is no 'Assign to me' shortcut.

items.item: An empty column shows a short message instead of blank space, a search or filter with no matches offers to clear it, and loading and failed-load (with retry) states exist
items.evidence: Empty columns do show 'No tickets' (page.html:175-180), but that text is generic and gives no 'clear search/filter' action when a search/filter yields zero matches; there is no loading state and no failed-load/retry UI anywhere in the markup or script — tickets are a hardcoded in-memory array with no fetch simulation.

items.item: Every relative time (such as "Updated 3h ago") also exposes the exact date, time and timezone, in a <time datetime> element or a title attribute
items.evidence: SLA labels are rendered as plain `<span>` text via sla.text (e.g. 'Due Nov 7, 2:00 PM', page.html:203) with no <time> element and no title attribute anywhere in the page; the string also omits year and timezone, and there is no other relative-time ('... ago') text in the page.

tells: gradient — header logo tile 'HD' uses a solid indigo square, but column status dots and SLA banner rely on flat Tailwind palette colors with no gradients; no gradient tells found
initials-avatar-non-person — assignee avatars (e.g. 'PS', 'MW', '?') are fine since they represent people/unassigned, not a tell
rainbow-status — STATUSES array assigns a distinct colored dot per column (sky, indigo, amber, emerald, slate: page.html:52-58), a multi-hue status-by-color scheme across the whole board
oversized-radius — board columns use rounded-xl (12px) per audit.json radius-scale violation (`div#board > div.flex.flex-col:nth-of-type(1)` actual 12px, expected ≤8px)
hover-lift — cards use `hover:shadow-md transition-shadow` (page.html:188) for a lift-style hover effect
card-in-card — ticket cards (bg-white, rounded-lg, shadow) sit inside column containers (bg-slate-50, rounded-xl, border) which sit inside the board, a nested card-in-card surface pattern
emoji-icon — SLA breach banner text uses a literal '⚠' emoji character (page.html:245) instead of an icon component
notes: Core CRUD/drag interactions (status change via drag, assignee/status edit via modal) work, and the empty-column and basic search/assignee-filter features are implemented, but most of the SLA-specific, ordering, accessibility, and empty/loading-state requirements in the checklist are not implemented. Audit.json also independently flags text-contrast failures (card ID and SLA label text, as low as 2.34:1) and a radius-scale violation on the column container.
